e: The date is usually a period (“1st–2nd century AD”); the inscription’s weight is spread evenly over the 25-year bands of the period, as on the “Building activity over time” card. The “more precisely dated” view shows only inscriptions whose dating spans at most 100 years.

Within the map area, Rome’s archaeological register (SITAR) records 1329 construction phases dated by the excavators (walls, foundations, floors; modern layers excluded); 1225 of them fall between 800 BC and AD 800. The date is usually a period, for example “1st century AD”. In that case the unit’s weight is spread evenly over the 25-year bands of the period, so each unit counts as one in total (aoristic method). The “more precisely dated” view shows only phases whose dating spans at most 100 years.
